journey.title: Tab away after typing an unavailable delivery date
journey.goal: Leaving the date field with Tab closes the calendar even when the typed date is outside the delivery window

steps.title: Type a date outside the delivery window

functionalJourney.title: Move the delivery into June with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking through the calendar to June and choosing a day fills the delivery date

guards.title: Type a valid delivery date and Tab away
guards.goal: A correctly typed date is committed and the calendar closes when the user tabs away

plan.root_cause: The datepicker does not hide on blur when the entered date is outside the allowed range, because the update/setDate logic early exits without hiding and no blur listener is registered to close the picker.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a blur event listener to the input field that calls this.hide() to ensure the datepicker closes when the input loses focus, regardless of validation outcome.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Ensures keyboard users can navigate away from the date field using Tab and the datepicker calendar will close, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Hiding the picker on blur may affect workflows where users expect the picker to remain open while interacting with other controls, but this aligns with typical datepicker behavior.
verification_requirements: After edit, typing a valid or invalid date and pressing Tab results in the datepicker closing (.datepicker not visible) and focus moving to the next element.
Selecting a date from the picker and then tabbing away also closes the picker.
All existing date selection and navigation functionality remains intact.

plan.root_cause: The datepicker does not hide on blur when the entered date is outside the allowed range, because the update/setDate logic early exits without hiding and no blur listener is registered to close the picker. Additionally, the input field is not updated with the last valid date on blur.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a blur event listener to the input field that calls this.update() to refresh the input field with the last valid selection (or the typed date if valid) and this.hide() to ensure the datepicker closes regardless of validation outcome.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Ensures keyboard users can navigate away from the date field using Tab and the datepicker calendar will close, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order). The input field will show a valid date.
functional_risks: Hiding the picker on blur may affect workflows where users expect the picker to remain open while interacting with other controls, but this aligns with typical datepicker behavior.
Calling update on blur may cause the selection to change if the typed date is valid, which is intended.
verification_requirements: After edit, typing a valid or invalid date and pressing Tab results in the datepicker closing (.datepicker not visible) and focus moving to the next element.
The input field displays a valid date (the typed date if valid, otherwise the previous valid date).
Selecting a date from the picker and then tabbing away also closes the picker.
All existing date selection and navigation functionality remains intact.
